resources.string: You are signed in with an API key. Single sign-on, host names and trusted proxies can only be changed after signing in with a password.
Only the owner can change this.
Sign in with your password to change this.
Make and revoke them on the API page
4 to 64 characters, for new passwords only

Short passwords are easy to guess. HolyArrs slows down repeated wrong sign-ins, which helps, but it does not make a short password safe. If HolyArrs can be reached from outside your home, use 8 or more.
An admin without it can open only My account until they turn it on. Anyone can turn it on for themselves in My account.
Show Forgot password? on the sign-in page
The owner gets a one-time code from the server log. Turn it off if people sign in through single sign-on. The reset-owner command still works.
People sign in with their Plex account on Plex\'s own page; HolyArrs never sees their Plex password.
People sign in with the name and password they use on your %1$s server; HolyArrs checks them with the server and keeps neither.
Show the %1$s button on the sign-in page
Link Plex to pick your server and import its people
Confirm on the Plex page that opened. This waits up to 10 minutes.
Linked. Pick the server people must share, then save.
Linked. Plex lists no server you own.
The Plex sign-in timed out. Start again.
The Plex sign-in has ended. Start again.
This Plex account is already linked to another HolyArrs person.
Too many Plex sign-ins were started. Wait a few minutes and try again.
Importing people from Plex stops working.
Only people it\'s shared with can join
Who may join the first time
New people join as Members. Plex managed users join as Kid (up to PG).
Only the names or emails below
Everyone with a Plex account (who shares the server, when set)
Everyone with an account on the %1$s server
Names or emails, one per line
This lets %1$s make a HolyArrs account the first time they sign in%2$s. They join as Members who may request titles.
everyone your Plex server is shared with
everyone with an account on your %1$s server
Sign in once as an admin of your %1$s server to list its people. HolyArrs ends that session right after and keeps neither the name nor the password.
People join as Members. Kid is PG or lower. Server admins stay Members.
The server restricts these accounts: %1$s. They will be added without the Kid limit.
A Sign in with single sign-on button for an OpenID Connect provider, such as Authentik, Authelia or Keycloak. Linked people sign in with their provider account; the owner keeps a HolyArrs password.
Confirm your password to open the single sign-on setup.
Single sign-on can only be set up after signing in with a password, not with an API key.
Set in the environment (HOLYARRS_OIDC_*), so it is only shown here. Change it where HolyArrs starts.
Show the single sign-on button on the sign-in page
The provider\'s issuer address, exactly as it publishes it (https://).
A secret is saved; it is never shown. Leave this empty to keep it.
Kept encrypted and never shown again.
Public client (no secret; the provider is set up for that)
Register this exact address at the provider.
New people the provider signs in may join, as Members who may ask for titles
The claim your provider puts groups in, often groups. Leave it empty to set roles only in HolyArrs.
Write group=role, comma separated, for example admins=admin, family=member. Each sign-in sets the highest role; people in none of these groups are Members. The owner never changes.
Yes, let everyone this provider signs in make an account here
Not on https://, so the secret is sent unencrypted. Use your https address.
Only if you use two-factor sign-in.
Type the client secret again, or switch on Public client: a saved secret never goes to a new issuer or client id.
Tick the box to confirm that everyone this provider signs in may join.
The password or code is wrong.
Trusted proxy sign-in: %1$s. It is set only in the environment (HOLYARRS_FORWARD_AUTH_*), because the addresses it trusts decide who may sign in as anyone.
Skip sign-in on my local network
Devices on your home network open HolyArrs without a password. Keys and passwords still need a sign-in.
People also sign in with %1$s. Skipping sign-in at home lets in only the person picked below.
The person picked here was removed or turned off, so everyone signs in. Pick someone else.
A Kid account or an age-limited invite exists, so only a Kid can open HolyArrs at home. Until you pick one, everyone signs in.
That\'s Docker\'s bridge, so HolyArrs can\'t tell home from outside. Until Docker passes real addresses, everyone signs in with a password.
Run the container with network_mode: host, or open HolyArrs through a reverse proxy and add the proxy under Trusted proxies.
Home visits arrive through Docker\'s bridge (%1$s)

HolyArrs counts this address as home while the skip is on, so opening it by the server\'s IP skips sign-in. Anything that reaches the server directly counts as home too, so don\'t forward this port to the internet.
A proxy in front of HolyArrs is not trusted, so sign-in is never skipped through it. Add the proxy\'s address to HOLYARRS_TRUSTED_PROXIES in the container settings.
Pick a Kid account if children use this network. If that person is removed, everyone signs in again.
One per line, like 192.168.1.0/24. Up to 32.
After / comes a number from 8 to 32
Too wide. List your home network, like 192.168.1.0/24
This is Docker\'s bridge, so everyone would get in
You\'re at %1$s · Docker\'s bridge, counted as home
%1$s · only if you\'re the only one on your Tailscale network
Only these can say where a visit came from.

Names you open HolyArrs by besides its IP address, like tower.local or media.example.com. The name you used at first-run setup is already here. Names in HOLYARRS_ALLOWED_HOSTS always work and are not listed.
Host names can only be changed after signing in with a password, not with an API key.
Set when HolyArrs starts, not here: list your reverse proxy addresses in HOLYARRS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and extra host names in HOLYARRS_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Without a proxy, nothing is needed.
Trusted proxies can only be changed after signing in with a password, not with an API key.

plurals.item: Saving a new issuer or client id removes the %1$d linked sign-in made through the old one and signs out everyone who used single sign-on. They link again from My account.
Saving a new issuer or client id removes the %1$d linked sign-ins made through the old one and signs out everyone who used single sign-on. They link again from My account.
